content: The server racks hummed like a chorus of the damned, their blinking LEDs casting a sickly blue glow over the cold concrete floor. I leaned against a towering blade chassis, the heat radiating off it like the last breath of a dying man, while the air conditioning wheezed its mechanical prayers into the stale air. Across the aisle, the sysadmin—pale as a ghost in a cheap suit—clutched a flash drive like it was the last bullet in his gun, his eyes darting between the security cameras and the emergency exit. "They’re already in the logs," he muttered, voice cracking. "You don’t understand what’s on this thing." I lit a cigarette, the flare of the lighter cutting through the gloom for a second before the smoke curled into the shadows. Somewhere in the labyrinth of cables and code, something was watching. And it wasn’t human.
